title: Chemistry — Atoms, elements and compounds
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for KS3 Science (chemistry) (status of the source: authored-reviewed-reverified-2026-10-08). Terms and clues: C2#c03 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C2#c04 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition; C2.1#xt1 term and clue written for the game; C2#c05 bank term, first sentence of the bank's definition. Questions: C2#q01, C2#q06, C2#q02, C2#q07, C2#q03, C2#q09, C2#q21, C2#x02 (written for the game), C2#x01 (written for the game).

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Chemical reaction
items.clue: A change in which new substances are made.

items.label: Element
items.clue: A substance made of only one type of atom.

items.label: Indivisible
items.clue: Unable to be split into anything smaller, as early models said of atoms

items.label: Molecule
items.clue: A particle made of two or more atoms chemically joined (bonded) together.

questions.stem: Which idea is part of Dalton's atomic model?

options.text: An atom has the colour of its element
Atoms can be seen with a light microscope
All atoms of one element are identical
Atoms are destroyed when things burn

questions.explanation: Yes. In Dalton's model every atom of one element is the same, and atoms of different elements are different (they have different masses). He also said atoms cannot be broken down, made or destroyed.

questions.stem: Which statement is true of every molecule?

options.text: It contains atoms of two different elements
It is two or more atoms joined together
It is just another word for an atom
It can be seen with a light microscope

questions.explanation: Yes. A molecule is two or more atoms joined (bonded) together. The atoms can be the same, as in O₂, or different, as in H₂O.

questions.stem: Hydrogen burns in oxygen to make water. In Dalton's model, what happens to the hydrogen atoms?

options.text: They are destroyed as the hydrogen burns
They become joined to oxygen atoms
They merge with oxygen into water atoms
They become wet, like the water made

questions.explanation: Yes. In Dalton's model atoms are rearranged, never made or destroyed, so the hydrogen atoms end up joined to oxygen atoms. Today we know each water molecule has two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.

questions.stem: Which of these is a compound?

options.text: Oxygen gas, O₂
Air in a jar
Pure water, H₂O
Salt solution

questions.explanation: Yes. Pure water, H₂O, is a compound: hydrogen and oxygen atoms are chemically joined in a fixed ratio of 2 to 1.

questions.stem: Under a school microscope, sulfur powder looks like tiny yellow grains. Which statement about one grain is correct?

options.text: It is one single atom of sulfur
It is made of atoms that are yellow
It is solid sulfur with no atoms in it
It contains a huge number of atoms

questions.explanation: Yes. Atoms are far too small to see, so even a tiny grain contains a huge number of sulfur atoms. The yellow colour belongs to the grain, not to a single atom.

questions.stem: Hydrogen burns, and oxygen helps things burn. They react to make water, which does neither. What does this show?

options.text: The atoms were destroyed in the reaction
The atoms changed into new water atoms
Water has too little hydrogen to burn
A new substance with its own properties formed

questions.explanation: Yes. Water is a compound, a new substance whose properties are different from those of hydrogen and oxygen. The atoms are the same ones, now joined in a new way.

questions.stem: In Dalton's model, what happens if you keep cutting a piece of copper into smaller and smaller bits?

options.text: You can keep cutting smaller bits for ever
You reach tiny orange, bendy copper atoms
You reach atoms that cannot be split
You reach atoms visible in a light microscope

questions.explanation: Yes. In Dalton's model, matter is made of tiny atoms that cannot be broken down. Cutting stops at single copper atoms.

questions.stem: Oxygen gas is made of O₂ molecules, each with two atoms joined together. Why is oxygen an element and not a compound?

options.text: Its molecules each contain just a single atom
Its molecules contain only one type of atom
Its molecules are not mixed with any other gas
Its molecules are far apart, because it is a gas

questions.explanation: An element contains only one type of atom, even when its atoms are joined in molecules.

questions.stem: In Dalton's atomic model, how do the atoms of gold compare with the atoms of iron?

options.text: They are the same kind, but packed more tightly
They are the same kind, but gold has more of them
They are yellow and shiny, unlike iron atoms
They are a different kind, with a different mass

questions.explanation: Dalton said all atoms of one element are identical, and differ from the atoms of every other element.
